items.item: Each row shows the user's name and email, role, status in words (such as Active, Invited, Deactivated, Locked) and whether two-factor sign-in is enabled
items.evidence: Row template (`$('rows').innerHTML = rows.map(...)`) renders avatar+name, email `mailto:` link, role text, status pill (`TONE[x.status]`), and last sign-in — there is no 2FA column, badge, or data field (`u()` objects only carry id/name/email/role/status/lastSignIn/you). Two-factor enablement is never shown.

items.item: Last sign-in uses one date-time format with the timezone stated, relative times also expose the exact time, and an account that has never signed in shows "Never" rather than a blank or a 1970 date
items.evidence: fmtAbsolute formats via `Intl.DateTimeFormat(LOCALE,{day,month,year})`/`timeFmt` with no `timeZone` option and no timezone label rendered anywhere (e.g. first.png shows "11/07/2026, 10:42 PM · 18 minutes ago" with no zone). `fmtLastSignIn` returns `'—'` for null lastSignIn instead of the word "Never".

items.item: Users can be found by searching name or email and filtered by role, status and inactivity (such as no sign-in for 90+ days), with the number of matching users shown
items.evidence: `#q` search and `#f-role` select plus status tabs (`renderTabs`) filter via `matching()`, and `#result-count` shows the count ("26 users"). But there is no inactivity/no-sign-in-90+-days filter anywhere in the UI or in `matching()`'s predicate.

items.item: The invite form requires an email and a role, labels both fields, and shows an inline error for a malformed address or one that already has an account
items.evidence: `<label for="inv-email">Email *</label>` / `<label for="inv-role">Role *</label>`; submit handler validates `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/` showing 'Enter an email like name@company.com', and checks `users.find(x=>x.email.toLowerCase()===email.toLowerCase())` showing 'Email already used by ${existing.name}' via `fieldError()`.

items.item: Deactivation asks for confirmation that names the user and states the effect (active sessions ended, sign-in blocked, data kept), and a deactivated user is offered Reactivate instead
items.evidence: confirmDeactivateOne text is only "${x.name} will immediately lose access to Acme Admin. You can reactivate the account later." — names the user and implies reactivation, but never states sessions are ended or that data is kept. Reactivate action itself does exist for Deactivated rows (`rowActions` returns `['reactivate','Reactivate']`).

items.item: The signed-in administrator's own row is marked (such as "You") and cannot be deactivated or lose the admin role, and the last remaining administrator cannot be deactivated, with the disabled action explaining why
items.evidence: Avery Chen's row shows "(you)" and `rowActions()` omits 'deactivate' when `x.you`, so self cannot be deactivated. However there is no protection or disabled/explained state for the last remaining Administrator — e.g. Jordan Patel (the only other Administrator) can be freely deactivated via the menu with no admin-count check or messaging.

items.item: Password reset sends a reset link to the user's email address, which the confirmation names, and the administrator never sees, sets or types the new password
items.evidence: Menu action 'reset' calls `announce('Password reset link sent to ${x.email}.')`; there is no password input/field anywhere in the markup for the admin to view or type a password.

items.item: Row actions are buttons or a keyboard-operable menu whose accessible names include the user (such as "Actions for Mai Nguyen"), and the outcome of an action is announced in an aria-live or role="status" region
items.evidence: `<button data-menu="${x.id}" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Actions for ${x.name}">⋯</button>` and outcomes go to `<div id="toast" role="status" aria-live="polite">` via `announce()`.

items.item: A search with no matching users shows a message with a way to clear it, and loading and failed-load states with a retry exist
items.evidence: `[data-state="empty"]` shows "No users match these filters" with `#empty-action` = 'Clear filters'; `[data-state="loading"]` has `aria-busy="true"` with skeleton rows; `[data-state="error"]` has `role="alert"` text 'Users could not be loaded.' plus `#retry` button.

notes: Overall a clean, non-templated build (audit.json score 100/100, no stock dashboard chrome like greeting headers, KPI tiles, gradients, or glass panels). Functional gaps are the main issues: no 2FA indicator, no stated timezone, 'Never' not used for null sign-in, no inactivity filter, incomplete deactivation-effect copy, and no last-admin protection.
